title: A sentence reporting NO bugs fails the report gate, destroying the whole session
body:
## What happens

`report_issue_consistency` scans report prose for a severity token (`/\bS[0-4]\b/`) and requires each
hit to have a **distinct matching `bugs[]` entry**. It has no notion of what the sentence is DOING,
so a sentence that reports the ABSENCE of bugs — while citing the severity of findings already listed
above it — is parsed as an unmatched finding and fails the whole report.

Observed on seed `1788728014` (build `b2a18856`, 131 turns, 9.9 min, $5.51). The player's prose:

    ## Bugs or design flaws
    No functional bugs found. Two minor clarity nuisances noted above, both S1.

The verifier's rejection, verbatim:

    ✗ blind report rejected: severity-bearing prose finding is missing a distinct matching
      bugs[] entry (S1: No functional bugs found. Two minor clarity nuisances noted above,
      both S1.)

**The player had already filed two matching S1 entries.** From the same report's structured
interview:

    bugs[]: [
      {"where": "Station dispatch board terminology vs. Tanner's Fever quest evidence-gathering",
       "severity": "S1", "note": "The word 'evidence' is reused for both the Station's report-slot
       category and unrelated in-quest physical clues…"},
      {"where": "Mid-quest checkpoint during The Tanner's Fever, right after taking the meadowsweet
       (decision 80)", "severity": "S1", "note": "The scheduled Continue/End checkpoint fired
       mid-quest and required switching to the parent overworld journey tool…"}
    ]

Two prose findings above, two matching structured entries, and a summary line. The only thing the
verifier could not match is the summary. Capture and envelope both succeeded; nothing else was wrong
with the run.

Receipt binding could not save it either, correctly — this failure class is not receipt-only:

    Receipt binding rejected: verifier failure is not receipt-only: severity-bearing prose
    finding is missing a distinct matching bugs[] entry…

## Why this is P1 rather than a curiosity

It is not a one-off, and it is not the player's mistake. Summarising is natural writing, and the
severity vocabulary is what the report format asks players to use — so the format invites exactly the
sentence that breaks it. Any player that writes "no bugs found, the two issues above are S1" loses a
completed session.

Same class, already in the corpus: seed `1788651590` (195 turns, 15.9 min, $11.79) was destroyed
because one `decisionProofHash` in its retention history had twelve characters dropped from the
middle while the player transcribed it. Different mechanism, identical outcome — a fully-played
session discarded at the report gate over form, not substance.

Both records are RETAINED in the corpus rather than quarantined, deliberately: quarantine is for
launch refusals and API kills, which say nothing about the game. These say something about the
harness, and deleting them would hide the rate.

## Acceptance

1. A severity token counts as a finding only when the sentence **introduces** one. A summary, a
   negation ("no functional bugs found"), or a reference to findings stated above does not.
2. The retained failed record's report (seed `1788728014`, at
   `ai-runs/playtest/runs/claude_code_seed1788728014_default.json`, `result` field) passes
   re-verification **unchanged** — no edit to the player's text.
3. Seed `1788651590`'s report is re-checked the same way, so the fix is measured against both losses
   rather than the newer one alone.
4. A regression pins BOTH directions: the false-positive summary sentence above must pass, and a
   genuine unmatched finding — a sentence that introduces an S2 with no corresponding `bugs[]` entry
   — must still fail. The second half matters more than the first: this check exists to stop a player
   describing a defect in prose and omitting it from the structured data, and that must keep working.

## Evidence

- `ai-runs/playtest/logs/claude_code_seed1788728014_default.runner.log` — the rejection as emitted.
- `ai-runs/playtest/runs/claude_code_seed1788728014_default.json` — the envelope carrying the exact
  report bytes and the structured interview quoted above.
- Store `/home/user/adventureforge-playtest/sessions`, 51 sessions; the two losses are
  `20260907T011249Z…70dc8fe51ef0` (this one) and the earlier `1788651590` record.

evidence.summary: report_issue_consistency requires every /\bS[0-4]\b/ token in report prose to have a distinct bugs[] entry, with no notion of what the sentence is doing, so a line stating the ABSENCE of findings while citing severities already listed is read as an unmatched finding. Two of 51 fully-played sessions (~$17 of play) destroyed for formatting that says nothing about the game.
